recap.text: Carl asks who runs the programme Vengeance of the Daughter. Zev says it is Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated, an entity from one of the center systems. The gentleman Zev dealt with was a Sac.

Zev tells Carl his contract with Sensation Entertainment remains in effect during Odette's show. Quasar bluffs Borant into granting a licence for Vengeance of the Daughter to continue past the sixth floor for an extra twenty percent. Sensation Entertainment agrees to the ninth-floor extension but waits a few days to sign, prompting Quasar to warn Carl to make the programme exciting.

Quasar warns Carl that a subsidiary of the Dream purchased Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated, and the new showrunners demand a third season. In a castle antechamber, Elite Herman the Fleet snaps a desk in half while covered in explosive satchels. Donut fires a Magic Missile at his face and Baroness Victory puts an axe through his head. Carl takes the body into his inventory.

beats.headline: A company from the center
beats.text: Carl wants to know who runs Vengeance of the Daughter, the programme he has just contracted with. Not a kua-tin outfit, Zev says: nobody in their system is allowed to run serials while the game runs, and in any case the nuances of scripted drama are lost on the average kua-tin. It is an entity called Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated, from one of the center systems, which tend to be more integrated. The gentleman she dealt with was a Sac. What is a Sac? Carl does not know, so she cannot tell him.
beats.gist: Carl asks who runs Vengeance of the Daughter, and Zev identifies the entity as Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated.

beats.headline: The contract outlives the floor
beats.text: Before the transfer to Odette's show, Zev passes on a message: the programme is still active, so Carl's contract regarding participation in any other programme is still in effect. If some other elite approaches, he is required to extract himself as best he can. The showrunners of other programmes generally honour the contract with Sensation Entertainment, and try to intervene on their end. A good-faith effort should be enough, though that is a question for his new attorney.
beats.gist: Zev tells Carl his contract with Sensation Entertainment remains active during the transfer to Odette's show.

beats.headline: A licence they never asked for
beats.text: In the negotiation with Borant, Quasar asks for one of the licences that let a secondary programme continue past the sixth floor, for Sensation Entertainment's Vengeance of the Daughter. It is an old rule: a showrunner running below expected profit may grant emergency use to a single programme, for an extra twenty percent to Borant. Borant agrees, provided it stays quiet. Quasar says the producers have already agreed. They have not; that is a bluff, and they have been unavailable. Carl's chaser gets an automated reply.
beats.gist: Quasar bluffs that Sensation Entertainment agreed to a license for Vengeance of the Daughter.

beats.headline: Yes, but not yet
beats.text: Zev reports that she is talking to the Sensation people, and that they mean to steer the narrative so the crawlers are back in a saferoom in time for Odette's show. Then Quasar's message, good news and bad: Sensation has agreed to accept Borant's offer of a ninth-floor extension, but they are being little bitches about it and want to wait a few days before signing anything officially. His reading between the lines: make the programme more exciting without throwing the star into the shadow, or they might decide to pull his plug.
beats.gist: Zev reports Sensation Entertainment intends to steer the narrative to return crawlers to a saferoom for Odette.

beats.headline: Under new ownership
beats.text: Quasar's message on arrival: remember that contract with Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated? The main character is dead and gone, but the guaranteed third season he and Carl negotiated is about to haunt the fuck out of them both. Sensation has just been purchased by a subsidiary of the Dream, and the owners are demanding their third season. Signet is not coming back, so whatever happens is going to be something stupid, and the new showrunners mean to use Carl's contractual obligation against him. Advice: stay away from any elites.
beats.gist: A subsidiary of the Dream purchased Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated and demands a third season.

beats.headline: Satchels under the shirt
beats.text: In a castle antechamber, Elite Herman the Fleet, ogre strongman, fights something inside himself, snaps a desk in half and tells Carl he was supposed to do it already. He is covered in explosive satchels. Donut fires a Magic Missile at his face and Baroness Victory puts an axe through his head; Carl takes the destabilising body into his inventory. Victory calls it an unlawful assassination attempt by Sensation Entertainment: the Dream, which now owns the company, was exerting undue influence on one of its elites. She is filing a grievance.
beats.gist: Donut and Baroness Victory kill Elite Herman the Fleet, and Carl inventories his explosive satchels.
